Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. To get the pilot sizing right for Elluminate, could you send a few quick data points (or drop the attached template back to me)? The specific items that will materially change the GPU footprint are below — the more granular the better (we typically use per-hour distribution for a 7‑day window):

- Average requests / minute (over last 30 days) and peak requests / minute (1-hour peak)
- Concurrent sessions: typical concurrency, P50, P95, P99 (if you have session IDs we can infer cookies)
- Prompt length distribution (tokens): P10/P50/P90 and heavy-tail examples
- Response length distribution (tokens) and any hallucination mitigation that inflates tokens
- Session type mix: single-turn API calls vs multi-turn chat (percentages)
- KV/Context reuse: estimate percentage of requests that hit cached prefixes (this changes KV cache pressure a lot)
- Percent of requests that include function/tool calls or large binary payloads
- Expected burst profile: multiplier (e.g., 3x baseline) and typical burst duration (minutes) and frequency (per week/month)
- Preferred latency SLOs (p95 and p99) and acceptable P99 tail (ms)
- Any restrictions (no offload to other regions, quantization limits, compliance constraints)

Attached: sizing-template-elluminate.xlsx — fill whatever you have and attach a short sample of production telemetry if possible (session_samples_q1.csv is ideal). If you don’t have all fields, even a 48-hour slice helps us run a quick simulation.

Goal: produce a recommended dedicated GPU footprint + a low-risk canary plan that meets your p95 latency target and stays under your cost envelope for the initial pilot.

I’m available for a short follow-up workshop next week to walk through the template.

Thanks,

Jonas — ran a quick simulation off the session_samples_q1.csv and the numbers below are my working recommendation for a conservative pilot footprint. I saved the short notes as initial-sizer-notes.pdf.

Summary recommendation (pilot, 30 days):
- Starting dedicated footprint: 6 x A100-40GB equivalent GPUs (we estimate this approximates 4x A100-80GB capacity for KV cache sizing on our runtime).
- Burst buffer: provision an additional 2 GPU equivalents as burstable capacity (auto-burst to these during 3x events). Configure burst throttles to protect p99 by quick-failing to a smaller model if sustained >5 minutes.
- Autoscale policy: base target occupancy 65% to reserve headroom for cold-cold cache misses; scale thresholds at 75% occupancy with 20s cooldowns for ramp-downs.

Assumptions I used (call these out in the workshop):
- Average total tokens / request: 220 tokens (prompt + response) based on provided distributions; heavy file summarize flows treated as 1.5% of requests with 1,200 avg tokens
- KV hit scenario: 38% hit assumed; if KV-hit drops below 25% we see ~15–20% more GPU time due to longer KV fetch/assembly
- Model families: recommend Redwood-GPT-4-8k-quant (primary) — quantized path gives ~1.9x throughput vs fp16 with 8–12% quality delta for your use-case; fallback: Redwood-GPT-3.5-extended for degraded tail handling (lower cost, faster cold-start)
- Latency targets: p95 < 300ms looks achievable at the proposed footprint with continuous batching tuned to 40–60ms batch latency. Expect p99 in 600–800ms range during burst tail.

Canary plan (high level):
1) Week 0: deploy a 1-GPU canary with representative traffic replay from the sample CSV (validate end-to-end infra and tracing).
2) Week 1: scale to 2–3 GPUs and enable KV cache warming jobs for top 10% of keys. Validate p95 baseline and end-to-end SLOs for chat flows.
3) Week 2: move to full pilot 6 GPUs + 2 burst; ramp traffic 20% steps across two business days. Monitor p95, p99, GPU occupancy, and token-econ.
4) Fallbacks: route excessive burst traffic to Redwood-GPT-3.5-extended and enable rate-limited queuing for non-critical calls.

Operational telemetry to monitor: p95/p99 latency, GPU occupancy per model, KV cache hit rate, batch latency, token/km cost per request, and function-call error rate.

Next steps for us: I can convert this into a short SOW appendix and an ops checklist for the pilot. Also recommend a 60‑minute workshop with their SREs to confirm traffic sampling and finalize reserved vs burst commitments.
